title: Removal of a Crew Mask Regulator from the Flight Deck Stowage Box
abstract: Removal of a crew mask regulator from the flight deck stowage box, with the oxygen system isolation and cleanliness controls that apply to any work on an oxygen line.

sections.purpose: This task removes a crew mask regulator from the stowage box at either pilot position or at the observer position, so that the regulator can be exchanged or the supply line can be worked on.
sections.job_setup_note: Oxygen work is a cleanliness discipline before it is a mechanical one. Every tool, glove and wipe used must be oxygen clean and free of hydrocarbon. Isolate the crew oxygen supply and vent the line before any connection is broken, and cap every open port immediately; an open oxygen port left uncapped for even a short time in a flight deck will pick up contamination from the ventilation flow.
sections.procedure: 1. Isolate the crew oxygen supply at the shut-off valve and confirm the position. WARNING: OXYGEN UNDER PRESSURE WILL IGNITE HYDROCARBON CONTAMINATION VIOLENTLY. USE ONLY OXYGEN CLEAN TOOLS AND GLOVES AND DO NOT USE ANY LUBRICANT THAT IS NOT OXYGEN APPROVED. 2. Vent the supply line at the vent point and confirm zero pressure at the gauge. 3. Get access in zones 211 and 223 by opening the stowage box at the affected position. 4. Disconnect the supply hose at the regulator and cap both ends immediately. CAUTION: CAP EVERY OPEN OXYGEN PORT AS SOON AS IT IS DISCONNECTED. AN UNCAPPED PORT IN A FLIGHT DECK PICKS UP CONTAMINATION FROM THE VENTILATION FLOW WITHIN MINUTES. 5. Disconnect the electrical connector at the actuator FIN 9HD where a demand sensor is fitted, and label it. 6. Remove the regulator retaining bolts EN436848-89 and keep them in the marked tray. 7. Lift the regulator D3510121814548 clear of the stowage box. 8. Remove the filter D3510124105324 at the inlet interface and discard it. 9. Inspect the stowage box mounting face for damage and for contamination. 10. Inspect the accumulator connection at FIN 77HE for security. 11. Put the regulator in its transport container with the ports capped. 12. Compare the installation with drawing D35101279146 and report any difference.
sections.close_out: Leave the supply line capped and the shut-off valve closed. Make an entry in the technical log that the crew oxygen system at the affected position is inoperative. Record the removed regulator serial number and the reason for removal, and send the used filter with the regulator if contamination is suspected.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 5 applies only where a demand sensor is fitted.

safety_precautions: Use only oxygen clean tools and gloves.
Vent the supply line and confirm zero pressure before disconnection.
Cap every open oxygen port immediately.
